title: Stability propagation checklist and weekly rollout binder (Apr 2028) - draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working binder for the "stability propagation" mini-release scheduled the week of 2028-04-09. Goal: introduce the runtime KV-cache update and two telemetry knobs (adaptive-batching v2, prefix-hint TTL) with minimal customer impact and a clear rollback path if latency or error rates regress.

Scope and constraints:
- Target services: hosted API + dedicated pools (us-west1, eu-west1).
- Hot-path change: KV-cache eviction priority order changed to time-first for long-running sessions.
- Low-risk changes: telemetry tag additions, internal metrics rename.
- Must preserve 99th percentile P99 latency SLO for text.generate route.
- No schema migration for customer data.

Quick owner & escalation map:
- Release lead: Aisha Chen (pager: +1-555-0199, slack: @aisha)
- Runtime lead: Marco Ruiz (@marco)
- Observability lead: Evelyn Park (@evelyn)
- SRE oncall: Team SRE rotation (primary: Samir Patel)
- Customer comms: Nora Li (CS)

Preflight checklist (must be green before gating):
- [ ] CI: all runtime unit tests & integration smoke (runtime PR 5482) pass in canary cluster
- [ ] Canary: 5% traffic on canary pool for 12h with automated telemetry sampling enabled
- [ ] Perf lab: 10k synthetic requests run (50/50 short/long seq) — p50/p95/p99 recorded
- [ ] Telemetry: new tags show up in prod traces and dashboards (prefix_hint TTL, adaptive_batch label)
- [ ] Cost estimate: Verify token cost delta < 3% (optics team sign off)
- [ ] Customer-impact check: run customer-sim job for top-10 customers using cached sessions
- [ ] Runbook updated in Confluence (linked in artifacts)
- [ ] Pager escalation list validated and calendar invites set for deployment window

Canary cadence (recommendation):
- Day 0 (Mon 04/09) 09:00 UTC: push runtime image with feature-flag default=off to canary nodes
- Day 0 10:00 UTC: enable feature-flag for 5% traffic (tag: canary-stability-2028-04)
- Day 0 18:00 UTC: review automated alarms (error rate, tail latency). If stable, increase to 15%
- Day 1 (Tue) 10:00 UTC: expand to 30% if no regressions observed
- Day 2 (Wed) 08:00 UTC: run long-tail soak for 24h with production traces sampled at 5%
- Day 3 (Thu) 09:00 UTC: decision meeting -> full rollout or rollback (15m)

Rollout calendar (concise week view):
- Mon 04/09: canary enable (5%) -> 15% if no issues by evening
- Tue 04/10: expand to 30% -> run perf lab batch
- Wed 04/11: soak + manual QA with solutions-engineering (customer-sim)
- Thu 04/12: decision; if good, start regional progressive ramp at 03:00 UTC
- Thu 04/12: us-west1 -> eu-west1 -> rest-of-world (staggered by 2h windows)
- Fri 04/13: final verification and customer comms digest

Guardrails and rollback triggers (hard stops):
- Error spike: > 0.5% increase in 5xx errors over baseline for any target route -> auto-throttle and decision meeting
- Latency regression: P99 of text.generate increases by > 15% sustained for >= 10m -> rollback to previous image in affected pool
- Cost shock: unexpected token cost > 10% or burst in GPU memory by > 8% -> pause rollout
- Telemetry gaps: if new tags or traces are absent for > 30m during canary -> halt and investigate

Rollback procedure (compact):
1) Set routing weight back to previous image via rollout tool (tag rollback-2028-04)
2) Disable feature-flag at control plane
3) Notify customer-success and ops (template below)
4) Run quick forensic job: compare kv-hit-rate, cache-evictions, and per-customer session-duration
5) Postmortem owner assigned within 24h

Post-release checks (first 72h):
- Hourly sampling dashboard: error rate, p50/p95/p99, kv-hit-rate, cache-eviction-rate
- Compare customer latency cohort: top-10 customers vs baseline (automated script)
- Verify adaptive_batch telemetry label presence and weight distribution endpoint logs
- Confirm no increase in retry storms (api-gateway metrics)

Release notes (draft) - short form for external customers:
Title: Stability propagation: improved KV-cache for long sessions + telemetry updates (Apr 2028)
Summary: This rollout updates KV-cache behavior to favor time-based eviction for long-running sessions, reduces cache churn for multi-turn flows, and introduces improved telemetry tags for batching and prefix-hints. Expected customer impact: typically lower latency for long multi-turn conversations; negligible change for single-turn calls.
Highlights:
- Runtime: KV-cache eviction prioritization change (time-first) to reduce mid-session KV churn
- Performance: adaptive-batching v2 telemetry (helps optimizer pick better batch sizes)
- Observability: new trace tags (prefix_hint_ttl, adaptive_batch_label) added
- Migration: no customer action required
Known issues (initial):
- Small subset of legacy session IDs (rare) might see a temporary extra cache miss on first rehydrate — observed <0.03% in canary
- Some internal dashboards will show renamed metrics for 48h while aggregation jobs catch up

Internal release-note appendix (changelog items):
- PR: runtime/#5482 - kv-evict: switch to time-first for sessions (>30m)
- PR: telemetry/#312 - add prefix_hint_ttl trace tag
- Linear: RELEASE-212 - rollout plan and gating checks

Communication templates:
- Internal ops alert (short): "Rolling back stability propagation in <region> due to P99 regression" — include deployment tag, time, and snapshot link
- Customer-facing (CS): friendly one-paragraph summary + link to release notes page; include customer impact checkbox

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Q: Should we include a fast-path config to force LRU for short sessions? (Marco to advise)
- Q: Are there any billing-metering implications for dedicated pools with KV-cache delta? (Finance ops)
- TODO: add Confluence link for full postmortem template
- TODO: drop a short video demo for solutions-eng to show before/after latency on a 10-turn chat

Safety checklist (final sign-off):
- [ ] Release lead gives green
- [ ] SRE oncall previewed escalation flow
- [ ] CS notified of possible affected customers (top-20)
- [ ] Post-release monitoring job scheduled (72h)

Appendix: quick commands and dashboards
- Rollout tool: /internal/rollout apply --tag canary-stability-2028-04 --weight 5
- Rollback tool: /internal/rollout rollback --tag rollback-2028-04 --region us-west1
- Perf script: scripts/perf/run_canary_batch.sh --seq-mix 50,50 --rps 200
- Dashboards: /dashboards/ops/kv-cache /dashboards/ops/text-generate-tail

If anything ambiguous in this doc, ping me on slack @aisha or add comments inline. This file is intentionally terse — fill in the numbered forensic queries after the first 24h of canary so we can run a short postmortem if needed.

-- Aisha (draft, work-in-progress)
